title: Negotiator: stochastic prefill kernel-compatibility scoring and safe-retract playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a Negotiator component in the serving runtime that performs a lightweight stochastic prefill negotiation between candidate model variants and kernel execution backends. The Negotiator computes a kernel-compatibility score and an early acceptance delta for short prefill probes, then decides whether to commit the faster speculative decoder path or to retract and fall back to the conservative decode path. Goals: reduce p50/p95 latency for common short-turn prompts, avoid quality regressions for high-risk prompts, and keep unit cost improvements when kernels are compatible. This ticket covers design, implementation plan, telemetry spec, and rollout strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator produces deterministic kernel-compatibility vectors for each probe and candidate model within 2 ms median overhead
When enabled, short-turn prompts (<64 prefill tokens) show >=10% reduction in p95 decode latency on the canary cluster without >1% drop in downstream BLEU/ROUGE/LLR-style quality signal
Fallback retract path triggers within 2 tokens of degraded acceptance score and preserves previous output correctness in at least 99% of triggered retractions in offline tests
Telemetry for negotiation decisions, kernel IDs, and per-decision acceptance_score is emitted and visible in Console dashboards
End-to-end integration tests for Negotiator+Decoder+Kernel selection exist and pass in CI for x86 and A100 kernels
tasks: Design scoring function for kernel-compatibility (kernel_fingerprint similarity + kernel latency prior) - spec doc
Implement Negotiator shim that runs a micro-prefill probe and aggregates candidate logits/kv-cache stats
Add acceptance_score field to request trace and wire through tracing/Console
Implement safe-retract: checkpoint prefill state, commit on acceptance, rollback and re-run conservative path on retract
Add feature flag and per-customer override in runtime config
Create integration tests and performance benchmarks across representative models and lengths
Run canary on dedicated pool with 1% traffic and monitor quality/latency metrics
decisions: Use a lightweight logistic model for acceptance_score (features: kernel_fingerprint_similarity, probe_ll_delta, prefill_length, kv_cache_hit_rate)
Checkpointing will use immutable prefills + kv-snapshot to allow O(1) rollback for small probes
Default policy: optimistic commit for mobile-like workloads (<64 tokens), conservative for long-context (>512)
rollout_plan: Developer testing on dev clusters with synthetic workload (immediate)
Canary: enable Negotiator for 1% of traffic on runtime-1.22 dedicated pool for 7 days
Quality gates: abort rollout if retract_rate > 2% or model.output_quality_delta < -0.5 LLR on canary
Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% by customer segment with per-customer opt-out
Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring window for regressions and cost accounting
runbook: If canary retract_rate spikes > 5%: disable Negotiator feature flag and rollback to last config
If acceptance_score distribution drifts: enable debug-level tracing for affected model+kernel and collect sample requests
If p95 latency increases > 10% for a customer: open ticket with SE and toggle their override to conservative path
Emergency manual override: Console button to set runtime.negotiator.enabled = false globally
notes: We purposefully keep the acceptance model simple to avoid heavy retraining cycles. Future iteration can promote a shard-aware learned policy when more safe telemetry is available.
